findings.title: Per-source disappearance is masked by duplicate event in another inbox
findings.expected: Reconcile previously observed source/event membership; quarantine disappearance and retain old cursor, even when another inbox still supplies identical event bytes.
findings.actual: Removing all events from the first inbox after observing the same events in two sources leaves both events verified, records result=verified and advances first cursor.
findings.impact: Source removal/history rewrite can be reported as a clean full scan. Original event bytes survive; this is a source-history detection gap, not demonstrated data loss.
findings.basis: PB-2 source disappearance/full reconciliation plus source registry historical membership. Current implementation compares a global identity union, not each retained source membership. Manager should confirm desired per-source semantics.

findings.title: Crash during first write poisons the content-addressed object path and blocks restart
findings.expected: A process crash before publishing state leaves prior state usable and permits the documented retry with old pin and the same authorized bytes.
findings.actual: A truncated file exists under its final digest name. After process restart, retry raises ValueError(object collision) before staging; the same operation cannot complete.
findings.impact: Knowledge delivery or scanning can become permanently blocked by a partial raw-object write until manual repair. No cursor corruption or development gate change was observed.
findings.basis: Real child process exits after a partial write and fsync, before state replacement. Fault injection substitutes only the raw-file write boundary. Product code is unchanged; normal restart uses production Store. Published five crash hooks all pass, but do not cover writes inside durable().

findings.title: Symlink/gitlink ancestor of inbox is accepted as empty
findings.expected: Reject unsafe Git ancestor modes while resolving the configured inbox prefix, including a symlink or gitlink above the final component.
findings.actual: Actual local fixed Git trees containing alias/events through a symlink ancestor, or module/events through a gitlink ancestor, return [] without rejection.
findings.impact: A first scan can treat an unsafe configured source as empty and advance its cursor. The links were not followed and no external content execution or disclosure was observed.
findings.basis: PB-2 fixed-source verification; supplied design section 8 expressly requires symlink/gitlink rejection. Existing tests cover leaf/exact-prefix links, but not ancestors.
